newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey scandal inquiry accuses government MPs.
newsitem.headline: Turkey scandal inquiry accuses government MPs.

text.p: A parliamentary investigation into a security scandal accused two Turkish government MPs on Friday of deep involvement in a network of shadowy links between top officials and right-wing gangsters.
"As far as politicians are concerned, Mehmet Agar and Sedat Bucak have been brought to light," chairman Mehmet Elkatmis told a news conference to announce the inquiry's findings.
The two deputies are members of the conservative True Path Party (DYP), in coalition with Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan's Islamists. The MPs deny breaking the law.
Agar resigned as interior minister last November shortly after the scandal broke when a senior policeman and a far-right gangster wanted for murder died in the same car in a traffic accident.
Bucak, who heads a tribal militia that fights Kurdish separatist rebels, was a passenger in the vehicle.

Newspapers printed frequent allegations after the crash that leading security officials and politicians used gangsters and drug smugglers for political dirty work, including the murders of Kurdish rebel sympathisers.
"There is dirty money, smuggling, terror and an international dimension," said Elkatmis, a deputy from Erbakan's Welfare Party.
Parliament does not have to act on the inquiry's findings.
A prosecutor has officially asked for the parliamentary immunity of Agar and Bucak to be lifted but the request has become caught up in red tape.
